nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

Copyright protects original creative works such as literary, artistic, musical, and software works. In India, copyright generally arises automatically when an original work is created;  but provides an official record of the claimed ownership and details of the work.
registration is not mandatory for protection
Taxswami assists individuals, creators, and businesses with the copyright registration process and related documentation.
Registration provides an official record of the copyright claim and particulars of the work.
Copyright gives the owner statutory rights over specified uses of the work.
Copyright can be licensed, assigned, or commercially exploited.
Registration records can be useful in enforcing rights and resolving disputes.
Copyright can form part of a business's intellectual property portfolio.
What Can Be Protected by Copyright?
Copyright protection may apply to original works including:
Books, articles, manuscripts, and other literary works
Computer software and certain digital works
Paintings, drawings, photographs, and other artistic works
Choreographic and other eligible creative works
Websites and other original digital content, where eligible

The application is submitted to the  in the prescribed form, along with the applicable government fee.
The application undergoes the prescribed process. Where objections or discrepancies arise, the applicant may be required to provide clarification or supporting documents.
If the application meets the applicable requirements and no unresolved objection prevents registration, the work is entered in the Register of Copyrights and the registration certificate is issued.
